summary: Assistance requested: Audit and safe escape for combined batching + kv-prefetch + int8 quant profile (BrightPost)
description:
Issue summary:
BrightPost enabled a combined optimization profile that turned on aggressive asynchronous batching, KV-prefetch for prefix caching, and an int8 quantization profile across their Dedicated pool. After the change they report increased 95th and 99th percentile latency and intermittent stream disconnects for chat endpoints. They request a guided audit of the current tenant config and a safe, low-risk escape hatch to restore stable latency without complete model reverts or data loss.

Impact:
- Customer-facing chat experiences show p95 latency rising from ~120ms to ~520ms for short prompts
- Some streaming sessions disconnect after ~12-18s when the request includes long context prefixes
- Revenue-impacting for their PLG usage during business hours in us-east region

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: brightpost-ded-01 (prod/us-east)
- Model pinned: redwood-v2-13b@2026-03-10
- Applied optimizer profile: brightpost-experiment-3 (batching=async-aggressive, kv_prefetch=enable, quant_profile=int8-agg-v1)

Steps to reproduce (as reported):
1) Send a streaming chat request with 512-token system prompt + 128-token user message to the chat endpoint.
2) Observe p95 latency and streaming stability for 20 parallel sessions.
3) Note disconnects after 12-18s for some sessions and occasional 502/504s in the console traces.

Attached/logs (snippets):
- Console trace (trace id bpost-20260313-7): "socket-closed: upstream read timeout after 17000ms"
- Serving runtime metric: "host:ded-01: p95_token_latency: 485ms, batch_size_98p: 54"
- Error excerpt: "rpc_error: Failed to allocate quant scratch buffer: OOM candidate on stream worker"

Customer request:
They asked for: (A) an audit of the active optimizer flags and a short checklist of non-disruptive toggles to attempt; (B) an immediate safe-escape sequence we can run that minimizes token-cost/regression risk; (C) validation steps to confirm success before unblocking full traffic.

Notes about precedence:
- They are on a Dedicated contract and prefer no model rollback.
- Traffic is production; preferred approach is per-tenant targeted changes or traffic-splitting rather than cluster-wide toggles.
comments: 2026-03-13 09:12 - Customer (Samir Kapoor): We flipped the optimizer profile yesterday evening and noticed latency surges this morning. Can you help us revert in a way that doesn't drop model pinning? We rely heavily on the cached prefixes for our personalization flows.

2026-03-13 09:35 - Support (Ava Patel): Thanks Samir — assigning engineering and SRE. Can you confirm the exact profile name and whether this was applied via Console or API? Also sending initial telemetry links to the team. (linked dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/ops/brightpost-ded-01)

2026-03-13 10:02 - Customer (Samir Kapoor): Profile: brightpost-experiment-3 applied from Console under Optimizer > Tenant Overrides. We did not change model pin. All traffic was live during the change.

2026-03-13 14:05 - SRE (Diego Morales): Observed increased batch sizes and higher memory pressure on worker hosts. Some workers entered retry loops when quant scratch allocation failed. Proposing per-tenant kv-prefetch disable as first pass and switch batching from async-aggressive -> async-moderate. Marking as P1 given customer revenue impact.

2026-03-14 08:21 - Engineering (Lin Zhao): Suggested safe operation: (1) apply tenant-scoped optimizer snapshot rollback for kv_prefetch only -> monitor p95 for 15 minutes; (2) if stable, scale batching down; (3) if still unstable, transiently redirect 30% traffic to a non-optimized variant using traffic-split route. Will provide exact API calls.
2026-03-14 09:12 - Support (Ava Patel): Sent step-by-step escape instructions to customer and scheduled a 9:30 UTC window to apply changes with them on call.
investigation_notes: Telemetry summary: p95 token latency increased from 120ms (baseline) to 480-520ms after profile applied. Memory RSS on hosts increased by +24% during peak. Error rate rose from 0.4% to 2.3% (502/504).

Root hypothesis: kv-prefetch increases memory working set for long prefixes; combined with aggressive async batching and int8 memory layout, some stream workers hit transient allocation failures leading to timeouts and stream disconnects.

Corroborating evidence: stack traces show repeated 'Failed to allocate quant scratch buffer' and runtime logs indicate batch coalescing produced batches >48 tokens frequently, higher than expected for this workload. Dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/d/ops/host-metrics?pool=brightpost-ded-01

Quick check run: toggled kv_prefetch=false in a single canary worker process (non-tenant-scoped) — observed immediate drop in p95 for requests hitting that worker (sample of 50 requests). This supports the kv-prefetch hypothesis.

Risks: toggling quant profile (int8 -> fp16) carries correctness risk for output distribution; full quant rollback would increase cost. Preferred minimal approach: disable kv_prefetch per-tenant then tune batching aggressiveness.
resolution_notes: Action taken (2026-03-14 09:35 UTC): Applied tenant-scoped change: set optimizer flag 'kv_prefetch' -> false for tenant BrightPost via API (tenant override). This change was scoped to the tenant and targeted the dedicated pool 'brightpost-ded-01'.
Validation (09:50 UTC): Observed p95 fall to ~150-170ms within 10 minutes for targeted flows. Streaming disconnects dropped to baseline. No model pin or quant profile was modified.

Follow-up: Rolled batching from 'async-aggressive' to 'async-moderate' for the tenant as a second step (09:55 UTC). This further stabilized memory pressure on worker hosts and reduced batch_size_98p to ~30.

Customer feedback (Samir, 10:10 UTC): Confirmed their front-end showed restored experience. They requested documentation of the safe-escape procedure and a plan to re-run an optimizer test with telemetry gates in place.

Permanent remediation recommendations: (1) Introduce per-tenant preflight simulator that runs new optimizer profiles against a small traffic shadow to check memory and batch-size distributions; (2) Add an automatic heuristic to block kv_prefetch when prefix lengths exceed a configurable threshold for dedicated pools; (3) Create a Console shortcut for one-click tenant-scoped 'optimizer safe-escape' that performs the exact steps we executed.
Ticket status: Waiting on customer to confirm post-incident telemetry retention and to schedule a follow-up session for re-introducing optimizations behind canary traffic-split and simulator checks.
